---
title: "Baseline DSA (Output 1)"
guide-section: "User Guide"
---

Excel analogues: **Baseline - external**, **Baseline - public**, Output 1-1,
and Output 1-2. Edit Ext, Macro, and Input 4/5 in Excel, save, then run
`load_core`.

> Excel → `load_core` → `external_dsa_panel` / `public_dsa_panel`

## Load and compute

```python
from pathlib import Path

from lic_dsf.load import load_core
from lic_dsf.output import external_dsa_panel, public_dsa_panel

workbook = Path("data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx")
macro, external, ext_base, pub_base = load_core(workbook)

out_1_1 = external_dsa_panel(ext_base)
out_1_2 = public_dsa_panel(pub_base)
```

Output 1-1 contains the external PPG debt PV and debt-service ratios. Output
1-2 contains public debt, public debt PV, debt service, and gross financing
need ratios.

Use `output_11_table(ext_base)` and `output_12_table(pub_base)` when you need
full Excel-row geometry instead of the smaller economist panels.

## Inspect the loaded books

These are optional checks, not separate setup steps:

| Area | Loaded object | Useful checks |
|------|---------------|---------------|
| New MLT instruments | `external.portfolio` | `pv()`, `new_debt_service()` |
| External debt | `external` | `total_pv_of_debt()`, `debt_evolution()`, `summary()` |
| Macro bridge | `macro` | `gdp_usd()`, `external_gfn()`, `public_gfn()`, `summary()` |
| Domestic indicators | `DomesticDebtBook(load_domestic(workbook))` | `domestic_debt_to_gdp()`, `domestic_ds_to_revenues()`, `summary()` |

`external.portfolio` covers new MLT instruments. Existing debt, short-term
debt, SDR allocations, and creditor aggregates remain on `external`.

## Excel cues

| Indicator | Baseline area |
|-----------|---------------|
| PV of PPG external debt / GDP | R35 |
| PPG debt service / exports | R39 |
| PV of public debt / GDP | R42 |
| Public GFN / GDP | R47 |

The complete worked example is
[`demo/baseline_dsa.ipynb`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/demo/baseline_dsa.ipynb).
